what_this_means_for_you.in_short: The second attempt at drawing parliamentary districts after BAA 58 was struck down - and itself overtaken by Supreme Court rulings. Like BAA 58, treat it as history: BAA 86 defines the districts actually used in the Sept 14, 2026 elections.
in_practice: Reconstituted districts after Sulu's exclusion from BARMM reshaped the region
Superseded in effect by BAA 86 following further Court action

for_specific_groups.Voters: Your operative district map is BAA 86
for_specific_groups.Court watchers: Read with the SC's 2025 districting decisions

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: All of BARMM unless the title names a specific place
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Laws take effect shortly after publication, but felt impact follows budgets, IRRs, and agency rollout - typically months, not days
what_you_can_do: Ask your municipal/barangay office or the implementing ministry how and when it will roll out where you live
Read the full text (PDF) on the Parliament's website or the Official Gazette of the Bangsamoro - the final sections say when it takes effect and who must act
If it isn't being implemented, raise it with your Member of Parliament or through the ministry's public assistance desk

key_terms_explained.BAA: Bangsamoro Autonomy Act - a regional law passed by the Bangsamoro Parliament, applying inside BARMM alongside national laws.
key_terms_explained.IRR: Implementing Rules and Regulations - the ministry-issued 'how-to' that turns a law's text into procedures; many laws only bite once the IRR is out.
key_terms_explained.GAA: General Appropriations Act - the annual budget law deciding how much each ministry and program gets.

benefits.headline: A real vote in choosing your own regional government.

direct_benefits.benefit: Your ballot elects the Bangsamoro Parliament on Sept 14, 2026 - district, party, and sectoral seats
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Register/verify with COMELEC; vote on election day

direct_benefits.benefit: Clear district representation: a specific representative answerable to your area
Sectoral seats give organized sectors (women, youth, ulama, IPs, etc.) guaranteed voices

indirect_benefits: Accountability: appointed transition officials give way to officials you can vote out
limitations: VOID/SUPERSEDED: Voided/affected by Supreme Court ruling on districting (Oct 2025); Parliament passed BAA 86 to comply. Benefits described applied only while operative.
Election laws confer process rights, not material benefits; their value is exercised at the precinct
